Electricity is used to generate a current through an iron core transformer.  
This current (50/60 Hz) is sent to heating coils connected to a three-phase or single-phase power supply, where it is converted into alternating heat above each heating element.  
This heat passes through the glass cooktop and is absorbed by the cookware placed on top, where it is transformed into thermal energy suitable for cooking food.  

Induction cooking consumes less electricity than conventional cooking appliances due to the high current used during induction, and since there is no open flame, it poses fewer safety risks associated with open flames and hot surfaces, such as hot dishes and utensils. The absence of an actual flame also helps prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.
